text: When the players change ends after the first game of a match, X says that the light from a window is shining into his eyes and asks for the match to be moved to the next table, which is not in use. The umpire should
options: report to the referee immediately
move to the adjacent table, provided the umpire considers that the request is justified
reject the request, but report to the referee after the match
reject the request because there was no protest during the previous game
correct: report to the referee immediately
note: Rule 3.3.1.2.10: The referee is responsible for deciding the acceptability of playing conditions.

text: The blade of the racket
options: must be flat and rigid and not more than 4mm thick
can be covered on a side used for striking the ball with sandwich rubber, with pimples in or out
must be covered on both sides with sandwich or pimpled rubber, with one side black and the other bright red
can be covered on a side used for striking the ball with pimpled rubber, with pimples in or out
correct: can be covered on a side used for striking the ball with sandwich rubber, with pimples in or out
note: Rule 2.4.1 / 2.4.3: There is no law regarding blade thickness; the blade doesn't have to be covered on both sides with rubber; pimpled rubber can only have pimples outward.

text: For international competitions
options: players are suggested to leave their rackets on the table between games
players are normally permitted to take their rackets with them between games
players can take their rackets with them between games only with the permission of the umpire
players must leave their rackets on the table between games
correct: players can take their rackets with them between games only with the permission of the umpire
note: Rule 3.4.2.5: Unless otherwise authorised by the umpire, players shall leave their rackets on the table during intervals.

text: A's racket makes a strange sound as he strikes the ball and on inspection it is found that there is a crack in the blade. The umpire should
options: allow A a few minutes to get another racket from the changing room
report to the referee
allow A to continue playing with the cracked racket since he says he has no other racket with him
require A to replace his racket immediately; report to the referee if A refuses
correct: require A to replace his racket immediately; report to the referee if A refuses
note: Rule 3.4.2.4: Since the blade is cracked it is no longer legal and must be replaced. It is not necessary to call the referee unless the player has no other racket immediately available.

text: The striking surface of the racket may be
options: covered with sandwich rubber, with pimples inward or outward, with a total thickness of sandwich rubber and adhesive being no more than 4 mm
covered with pimpled rubber, with pimples inward or outward, with a total thickness of rubber and adhesive being no more than 2 mm
plain wood, dark in colour, either naturally or by being stained but not painted
two of the other three answers presented are correct
correct: covered with sandwich rubber, with pimples inward or outward, with a total thickness of sandwich rubber and adhesive being no more than 4 mm
note: Rule 2.4.3: Pimpled rubber can only have pimples outward; the striking surface has to be covered with rubber.

text: At the start of the fourth individual match of a team match, the player enters the court with his spare racket and informs the umpire that he wants to use his spare racket instead of the racket used in his previous match. The umpire should
options: allow the player to use his spare racket and collect it after that match for racket testing in the Call Area or Racket Control Centre
not allow the player to use the spare racket because it was not tested in the Call Area prior to the start of the team match
not allow the player to use the spare racket because he can only replace his first racket if it is accidentally damaged so badly during the last match and can no longer be used
call the referee
correct: allow the player to use his spare racket and collect it after that match for racket testing in the Call Area or Racket Control Centre
note: Rule 3.4.2.4 refers to an individual match; players are allowed to change their racket during a team match.

text: Player X brings his racket to the Call Area before the start of his match. Both sides of his racket are covered with sandwich rubber. On checking the coverings, you find that the red covering is not in the LARC. The umpire should
options: not allow the racket to be used because one of the coverings is not in the LARC
allow the racket to be used but only if the black side is used for striking the ball
disqualify the player
allow X to use the racket if his opponent has no objection
correct: not allow the racket to be used because one of the coverings is not in the LARC
note: Rule 3.2.1.3: Any ordinary pimpled rubber or sandwich rubber covering the racket shall be currently authorised by the ITTF.

text: When they arrive for a doubles match, X/Y are wearing blue shirts, but A's is red, and B's is yellow. A/B say that they are from different Associations and that each is wearing his Association's designated colour. The umpire should
options: insist that A and B wear shirts of the same colour
report to the referee
allow them to wear different-coloured shirts anyway
allow them to wear different-coloured shirts as they are from different Associations
correct: allow them to wear different-coloured shirts anyway
note: Rule 3.2.2.7: Uniform dress is required only for team matches and for doubles pairs of the same Association in World, Olympic or Paralympic Title Competitions. Otherwise there is no requirement, so any reference to Association is irrelevant.

text: A protests that a watch X is wearing is so shiny that it is distracting him. X says that he wore the same watch in 3 earlier matches, and no one complained. The umpire should
options: ask X to remove or cover the watch whether he considers the protest is justified
ask X to remove or cover the watch if he considers the protest justified
reject the protest as the watch has been worn in previous matches without protest
report to the referee immediately
correct: ask X to remove or cover the watch whether he considers the protest is justified
note: HMO 8.4.7: The umpire should ask for brightly reflecting items to be covered or removed. If refused, the matter must be reported to the referee, whether or not the umpire supports the protest.

text: A's shirt is red. X initially wears a dark blue shirt, but he comes to the table for the 3rd game in a green shirt, saying that the blue one is too wet to wear and that he has no other spare shirt with him. The umpire should
options: insist that X continue playing in the blue shirt
allow X to wear the green shirt, provided the Competition Manager agrees to the change of colour
allow X to wear the green shirt, because its colour is still sufficiently different from that of A's
report to the referee
correct: allow X to wear the green shirt, because its colour is still sufficiently different from that of A's
note: HMO 8.1.6: If a player has to change a shirt during a match, the new shirt does not have to be the same colour, but must still comply with the clothing rules.

text: Which of the following playing clothing is not allowed?
options: light blue shirt without sleeves
orange shirt with white sleeves if playing with white balls
one-part sports outfit
green shirt with an advertisement for the local cigarette company on the sleeve
correct: green shirt with an advertisement for the local cigarette company on the sleeve
note: Rule 3.2.5.1.1: Advertisements on playing clothing shall not be for tobacco goods.

text: How many advertisements are allowed on the front, side or shoulder of a player's shirt?
options: 4 within a total area of 400 cm²
4 within a total area of 600 cm²
6 within a total area of 400 cm²
6 within a total area of 600 cm²
correct: 6 within a total area of 600 cm²
note: Rule 3.2.5.9.2: Not more than 6 clearly separated advertisements, within a combined total area of 600 cm², on the front, side or shoulder of a shirt.

text: Two players from different Associations are to play doubles together at an Open International Tournament and each has his own advisor during their match. Which of the following statements is true?
options: the two players should wear similar coloured shirts
the two players should each wear their own Association's uniform
if the advisor of one player is warned for illegal advice, this warning applies to the advisor of the other player as well
each advisor can advise his player only
correct: if the advisor of one player is warned for illegal advice, this warning applies to the advisor of the other player as well
note: Rule 3.5.1.2: Where the players of a doubles pair are from different Associations each may designate an adviser, but with regard to 3.5.1 and 3.5.2 these two advisers shall be treated as a unit.

text: At the start of a match, the winner of the toss can
options: choose an end, after which the opponent must serve first
ask the opponent to serve first
ask the opponent to make the first choice
ask the opponent to serve first and the opponent can then choose an end
correct: ask the opponent to serve first and the opponent can then choose an end
note: Rule 2.13.2: When one player or pair has chosen to serve or to receive first or to start at a particular end, the other player or pair shall have the other choice.

text: The ends of the net shall
options: be attached to the supporting posts from top to bottom
be as close as possible to the supporting posts
be as close as possible to the supporting posts so that the gap between the net and the post is not more than 20mm
be well supported
correct: be attached to the supporting posts from top to bottom
note: Rule 2.2.4: The ends of the net shall be attached to the supporting posts from top to bottom.

text: As A runs around the side of the table to return a ball which bounces near the net, he trips and falls to the floor. His body on the floor prevents X from reaching the ball and X does not make a good return. The umpire should
options: award a point to A because X did not make a good return
award a point to X because A prevented him from making a good return
declare a let because A would be unable to continue owing to the accident
declare a let because A accidentally prevented X from making a good return
correct: declare a let because A accidentally prevented X from making a good return
note: Rule 2.9.1.3: The rally shall be a let if failure to make a service or a return is due to a disturbance outside the control of the player.

text: X makes a good return and then stumbles and drops his racket. To steady himself, he rests the hand with which he had held the racket on the playing surface but does not move the table. A's return misses the table. The umpire should
options: award a point to A because X touched the playing surface with his free hand
take no action because the playing surface was not moved
award a point to A because X touched the playing surface with his racket hand
award a point to X because A did not make a good return
correct: award a point to A because X touched the playing surface with his free hand
note: Rule 2.10.1.11 / 2.5.6: The free hand is the hand not carrying the racket. In this case both hands of player X were free hands.

text: In doubles X served to A in the first game. At the start of the 2nd game, B serves to X and successive good returns are made by X and A. Y's next return misses the table and it is then realized that the order of server and receiver is wrong. The umpire should
options: award a point to A/B, because Y's return was not good, and continue with A serving to X
award a point to X/Y, because the wrong player served, and continue with A serving to X
award a point to A/B, because Y's return was not good, and continue with B serving to Y
declare a let, because the wrong player served, and continue with B serving to Y
correct: award a point to A/B, because Y's return was not good, and continue with B serving to Y
note: Rule 2.14.3: All points scored before the discovery of an error shall be reckoned. Rule 2.14.1: Play continues in the order chosen by the pair having the right to serve first in the game during which the error is discovered.

text: In the first game of a singles match, player A was given a warning for misbehaviour. In the second game, just as A was about to serve with the score at 8-1, A misbehaved again. Who is to serve next?
options: A to continue serving with the score at 8-1
A to continue serving with the score at 8-2
X to serve with the score at 2-8
X to serve with the score at 3-8
correct: X to serve with the score at 2-8
note: Rule 2.13.3: X is awarded 1 penalty point making the score 8-2, at which score it is X's turn to serve.

text: A, a left-handed shake-hand player often holds the racket with both hands when making a backhand return. During a rally, as A makes a backhand return whilst holding the racket with both hands, his right hand touches the playing surface. The umpire should
options: call 'let' and tell A that he cannot play with both hands holding the racket
call 'stop' and award a point to X, and tell A that he cannot play with both hands holding the racket
call 'stop' and award a point to X because A's free hand touched the table
take no action
correct: take no action
note: Rule 2.5.5: Holding the racket with both hands is allowable; both hands are then racket hands, so A has no free hand, the return is good and play continues.

text: In doubles, with the score at 7-6, it is realized that A, who has been serving to Y, should have been serving to X at that stage. Neither the umpire nor the players can remember when the error occurred, although they know the server was changed at score 5-5. The umpire should
options: continue match at 5-5 with A serving to X
continue match at existing score with A serving to X
continue match at existing score with A still serving to Y
replay game in which error was discovered and use correct serving sequence
correct: continue match at existing score with A serving to X
note: Rule 2.14.3: All points scored before the discovery of an error shall be reckoned. Rule 2.14.1: Play continues with the correct order for the game in which the error is discovered.

text: At the start of a doubles match, A serves to X. When the score is 6-4 in the 5th and final game, who should be serving to whom?
options: A serves to X
Y serves to B
X serves to A or Y serves to B
A serves to Y or B serves to X
correct: X serves to A or Y serves to B
note: In the 5th game either A served to X or B served to Y first. At 6-4 either X or Y is serving, and since it is the final game, the receiver changed when X/Y scored 5 points.

text: In an individual event, A's advisor signals for a time-out but A says he doesn't want one. The umpire should
options: allow a time-out of up to one minute, and A is not entitled to another time-out
not allow the time-out because the player has the final decision
allow a time-out, and because A is ready to play, the time-out is over immediately
allow the time-out and permit X to receive advice for not more than one minute
correct: not allow the time-out because the player has the final decision
note: Rule 3.4.4.2.2: If a player and an adviser disagree whether a time-out is to be taken, the final decision is made by the player or pair in an individual event and by the captain in a team event.

text: In an individual event a time-out
options: can be claimed once in a match by each player or pair, but not in the 1st game
can be called between games or between rallies in a game
can be claimed only by a player or pair and not by an advisor
can be called only between rallies in a game
correct: can be called only between rallies in a game
note: Rule 3.4.4.2.3: The request for a time-out can be made only between rallies in a game.

text: The referee may authorize a suspension
options: if a player is injured, but in no case may the suspension be longer than 10 minutes
if a player is injured, a suspension will normally not exceed 10 minutes but may be extended until all blood has been removed, even if it takes longer than 10 minutes
if a player is exhausted as a result of strenuous/exhausting play
if a player accidentally breaks his racket, he will be allowed not more than 10 minutes to repair it or find a replacement racket
correct: if a player is injured, a suspension will normally not exceed 10 minutes but may be extended until all blood has been removed, even if it takes longer than 10 minutes
note: Rule 3.4.4.6: If anyone in the playing area is bleeding, play shall be suspended immediately and shall not resume until that person has received medical treatment and all traces of blood have been removed.

text: After 4 closely fought games, the match score is 2-2 (2 games each). In the fifth game, A complains of dizziness brought on by his exertions/physical efforts in the match and asks for a suspension. The umpire should
options: stop the game and get medical attention for A, with the stoppage not to exceed 10 minutes
inform A that if he does not resume play immediately, the referee would be called and he could forfeit the match
report this to the referee
grant an emergency suspension of play, not to exceed 10 minutes
correct: inform A that if he does not resume play immediately, the referee would be called and he could forfeit the match
note: Rule 3.4.4.5: A suspension shall not be allowed for a disability due to the normal stress of play; cramp or exhaustion caused by the player's fitness or the manner in which play has proceeded does not justify an emergency suspension.

text: If a player is bleeding during a match, the umpire should
options: allow the injured player to rest for five minutes only
suspend the play until the injured player is treated by a medical official
let the match continue if the player says that he wants to finish the game as soon as possible
suspend play immediately until all traces of blood have been removed
correct: suspend play immediately until all traces of blood have been removed
note: Rule 3.4.4.6: If anyone in the playing area is bleeding, play shall be suspended immediately and shall not resume until that person has received medical treatment and all traces of blood have been removed from the playing area.

text: In a team match consisting of 4 singles and one doubles matches, B, after playing the previous singles match, asks for 10 minutes break before he plays in the doubles match, which is next. The umpire should
options: allow him 5 minutes whether the opponents agree
require him to play without delay because play must be continuous
allow him 10 minutes if the opponents agree
call for the referee
correct: allow him 5 minutes whether the opponents agree
note: Rule 3.4.4.3: A player who is required to play in successive matches of a team match may claim an interval of up to 5 minutes between those matches.

text: During an individual match play is continuous except for
options: an interval of 2 minutes between successive games
an interval of 1 minute between successive games
an interval of 5 minutes between the 3rd and 4th games in a match of the best of 5, and 1 minute between other successive games
an interval of 1 minute between successive games and other authorised intervals
correct: an interval of 1 minute between successive games and other authorised intervals
note: Rule 3.4.4.1.1: an interval of up to 1 minute between successive games; Rule 3.4.4.1.2: brief intervals for towelling after every 6 points and at the change of ends in the last possible game. Option b is only partially correct.

text: After every 6 points players are entitled to a brief interval for towelling. The assistant umpire, who is keeping time, should
options: take no action as the towel break is part of the playing time of a game
stop the watch as the towel break is not part of the playing time of a game
stop the watch, if she is of the opinion that the players are taking long towel breaks
comply with the referee's decision, which he or she will announce at the briefing before start of the tournament
correct: stop the watch as the towel break is not part of the playing time of a game
note: HMO Appendix A 14: Start the timer as the first player serves, stop, and re-start it for substantial breaks in play, such as time spent for towelling.

text: In a singles match played under very hot and humid conditions, player A (who wears spectacles) several times requests short breaks to dry his glasses with his towel. The umpire should
options: allow the short breaks as player A is entitled to dry his glasses whenever necessary
request player A to dry his glasses with his shirt only, except during the 6-points towelling break, so as not to delay the game
not allow the short breaks as play must be continuous
examine the spectacles himself to decide whether player A's glasses need to be dried or not
correct: allow the short breaks as player A is entitled to dry his glasses whenever necessary
note: HMO 13.3.2: Spectacle wearers can have particular problems, especially in hot conditions, and the umpire may allow them short breaks for cleaning between any rallies.

text: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: in doubles, each player of a pair is entitled to a warning for a doubtful service
if there is an assistant umpire, either the umpire or the assistant umpire can give a service warning
if there is an assistant umpire, only the umpire can give a service warning; the assistant umpire cannot give a service warning
if there is an assistant umpire, no service warning is issued
correct: if there is an assistant umpire, either the umpire or the assistant umpire can give a service warning
note: Rule 2.6.6.1: If either the umpire or the assistant umpire is not sure about the legality of a service he or she may, on the first occasion in a match, interrupt play and warn the server.

text: When A serves, the ball first hits the net post and then his side of the table, from where it spins over the net. Before it can bounce on X's side of the net, X catches it, above the table. The umpire should award a
options: point to A because X obstructed the ball
point to X because A did not make a good service
point to A because X prevented A from making a good service
let, because the ball was obstructed in a net-cord service, which was otherwise good
correct: point to X because A did not make a good service
note: Rule 2.6.3: Since the ball hit the net post before touching the table, the serve is not good.

text: X serves and the ball bounces on his court, touches the top of the net and goes high in the air. A catches it, above the playing surface, with his free hand, which he then rests on the playing surface. The umpire should award a
options: point to A because X did not make a good service
point to X because A's free hand touched the playing surface
point to X because A obstructed the ball
let, because the ball touched the net and was obstructed by A
correct: let, because the ball touched the net and was obstructed by A
note: Rule 2.9.1.1: The rally shall be a let if in service the ball touches the net assembly, provided the service is otherwise correct or the ball is obstructed by the receiver or his or her partner.

text: A stamps (heavily stamping on the floor) his foot each time he serves; X is disturbed by this, and the noise is loud enough to be offensive and annoying to the spectators. The umpire should
options: award a point to X as stomping a foot during a service is not permitted
report this to the referee
handle under the Point Penalty System (PPS) and give A a warning
call a let and warn A not to stamp his foot; report this to the referee if A stamps his foot again
correct: handle under the Point Penalty System (PPS) and give A a warning
note: Rule 3.5.2.1: Players and coaches or other advisers shall refrain from behaviour that may unfairly affect an opponent, offend spectators or bring the sport into disrepute.

text: In serving, A tries to strike the ball as it rises but misses it. He tries again as it falls and, when it is just below the level of the playing surface, he strikes it upwards so that it bounces from his court, over the net and onto X's court. X, taken by surprise, tries to return the ball but hits it into the net. The umpire should award a
options: let, because the ball was struck below the level of the playing surface
point to A because X did not make a good return
let, because X was not ready
point to X because the ball was struck below the level of the playing surface
correct: point to X because the ball was struck below the level of the playing surface
note: Rule 2.6.4: From the start of service until it is struck, the ball shall be above the level of the playing surface.

text: In a doubles service, the ball touches the server's right half court and then the net. The umpire should
options: immediately call net, then let if the ball touches the receiver's half court
wait until the ball touches the receiver's half court before calling let
raise her arm but wait for the ball to touch the court before making a call
wait for the ball to touch the correct court or not before calling let or fault
correct: wait for the ball to touch the correct court or not before calling let or fault
note: HMO Appendix C: When the ball touches the net during service, the umpire should wait until the ball touches the correct court or half-court and make the appropriate call.

text: The free hand, while in contact with the ball and at the instant of projecting the ball upwards, shall be
options: behind the server's left court end line
above the level of the playing surface and behind the server's end line
behind the server's right court end line
none of the other three answers presented are correct
correct: none of the other three answers presented are correct
note: Rule 2.6.4 refers to the position of the ball (above the playing surface, behind the end line, not hidden). There is no reference to the position of the free hand in service.

text: During a rally A strikes the ball while it is below the level of the table. It passes under the net assembly outside the table and then touches the playing surface on X's side. The umpire should
options: award a point to A
award a point to X
call a let
take no action
correct: take no action
note: Rule 2.7.1: The ball shall be struck so that it touches the opponent's court, either directly or after touching the net assembly. It is not necessary for the ball to go over the net.

text: At the score 6-6 in a doubles match, A should be serving to X. By mistake, B serves to X and successive good returns are made by X and A. The next return is made by Y, but the ball misses the table and goes out of play, when you (as umpire) realize that the wrong player served to start the rally. The umpire should award a
options: point to A/B, because Y's return was not good, and continue with A serving to X
point to X/Y, because the wrong player served, and continue with A serving to Y
point to A/B, because Y's return was not good, and continue with B serving to Y
let, because the wrong player served, and continue with A serving to X
correct: point to A/B, because Y's return was not good, and continue with A serving to X
note: Rule 2.14.3: All points scored before the discovery of an error shall be reckoned. Rule 2.14.1: Play continues in the correct order for the game in which the error is discovered.

text: At the start of the fifth game of a doubles match between A/B and X/Y, X served to B. Who should be serving and receiving after the players change ends with the score 2-5?
options: B to X
A to X
A to Y
Y to B
correct: A to Y
note: Initial order X-B-Y-A, so at 2-5 A is serving but the receiving order is reversed: A-Y-B-X.

text: With the score 4-2 in the last possible game of a doubles match, A serves to X and X misses the ball. Just after the ball touches the floor the time limit is reached. In the next rally
options: A serves to Y
X serves to B
X serves to A
Y serves to A
correct: X serves to A
note: Rule 2.15.3: If the ball is not in play when the expedite system comes into operation, play resumes with service by the player who received in the immediately preceding rally. X received in the previous rally, so X serves to A.

text: At the start of the final game of a doubles match, A serves to X. When the score is 2-6 in the final game, who could be serving to whom?
options: A to X
B to X
X to A
Y to B
correct: B to X
note: At 2-6 either A or B is serving: A to Y or B to X.

text: During the first game in a doubles match, A serves to X and the timekeeper calls 'time' during the rally. To start the next rally under the expedite rule
options: A serves to X
X serves to A
X serves to B
B serves to Y
correct: A serves to X
note: Rule 2.15.3: If the ball is in play when the time limit is reached, play shall be interrupted and resume with service by the player who served in the rally that was interrupted.

text: The umpire can call 'let' and warn a player the first time he makes an illegal service
options: only if no assistant umpire has been appointed
only if the assistant umpire says he could not see the service action
only if he is sure that the server gained no advantage
in no circumstances
correct: in no circumstances
note: Rule 2.6.6.1: A warning is possible only when the umpire or assistant umpire is not sure about the legality of a service. Here the service is illegal, not doubtful.

text: A return may be good if
options: the ball is struck by the racket handle then the blade in a continuous stroke
the ball goes under the projection of the net bracket beyond the table
the ball accidentally strikes first the finger, then the racket
all other answers presented are correct
correct: all other answers presented are correct
note: Rule 2.10.1.7: A point is lost only if a player deliberately strikes the ball more than once in succession. Rule 2.7.1: The ball shall be struck so that it touches the opponent's court. All returns are good.

text: A makes a good but very high return which X moves in to kill (smash); just then C wins his match on the adjoining table and lets out a victory yell which startles X so much that he misses the ball. The umpire should award a
options: point to A as X failed to make a good return
let, as the umpire decides that X missed the ball because of a disturbance beyond his control
point to X because he would have won it anyway
point to X only if A agrees he would have won it anyway; otherwise a let is called
correct: let, as the umpire decides that X missed the ball because of a disturbance beyond his control
note: Rule 2.9.1.3: The rally shall be a let if failure to make a return is due to a disturbance outside the control of the player.

text: Player A strikes the ball beyond the sideline after it has completely crossed the playing surface on his side without touching the table but before it crosses the end line. The umpire should
options: award a point to A
award a point to X
call a let
take no action
correct: award a point to A
note: Rule 2.10.1.4: A point is scored if the ball passes over the player's court or beyond his end line without touching his court. The ball is out of play as soon as it crosses the sideline.

text: During the first game of a match you warn X for shouting abuse at A, although this does not appear to bother A. In the second game X again shouts and physically threatens A when he loses a point. The umpire should
options: report to the referee immediately
warn X again for bad behaviour
hold up a yellow and a red card and award 1 point to A
take no action, provided you are sure that A is not being disturbed
correct: report to the referee immediately
note: Rule 3.5.2.2: For a serious offence the umpire shall suspend play and report immediately to the referee. Physically threatening an opponent is a serious offence.

text: Just as X is about to make a return shot, A shouts out loudly which causes X to miss the ball. The umpire should
options: call a let
call a let and give a yellow card to A for misbehaviour during the rally
call fault and give one penalty point to X
take no action
correct: call a let and give a yellow card to A for misbehaviour during the rally
note: Rule 2.9.1.3: Let for a disturbance outside the control of the player. Rule 3.5.2.2: Deliberate shouting is misbehaviour but not serious, so the Point Penalty System applies (yellow card).

text: A serves at the score 8-10. As the ball, returned by X, lands on the playing surface the match clock shows that 10 minutes have expired. The umpire should
options: call 'let' and continue under the expedite system with A serving
call 'let' and continue under the expedite system with X serving
allow play to continue but start the next game under the expedite system
allow play to continue and take no further action
correct: allow play to continue and take no further action
note: Rule 2.15.2: The expedite system shall not be introduced in a game if at least 18 points have been scored.

text: When the expedite system is in operation
options: the receiver wins the point if he makes twelve good returns counting the return of service as the first return
each player serves one point in turn; the stroke counter counts when the return is good
in singles the receiver of the last point in a game always serves the first point in the next game provided that the match is not over
none of the other three answers presented are correct
correct: none of the other three answers presented are correct
note: Rule 2.15.4: The receiver must make 13 correct returns. The stroke counter counts as soon as the ball is struck. Rule 2.15.5: Expedite does not alter the order of serving and receiving in the match.

text: In timing a match,
options: time should be started when the ball is first served and stopped at the end of each rally
the umpire or assistant umpire time the pre-match practice, each game, the intervals between games and any time-outs; time is stopped whenever the ball leaves the playing area

the assistant umpire times the pre-match practice, each game and the intervals between games, the umpire must time any time-outs. Time is stopped for any delay such as a long conversation between playing partners in doubles

the umpire or assistant umpire time the pre-match practice, each game, the intervals between games and any time-outs. Time is stopped whenever the ball leaves the playing area and any delay such as a long conversation between playing partners in doubles
correct: the umpire or assistant umpire time the pre-match practice, each game, the intervals between games and any time-outs; time is stopped whenever the ball leaves the playing area
note: Rule 3.3.2.5.5: Either the umpire or the assistant umpire may time the practice period, play and intervals. HMO Appendix A 14: Stop the timer for substantial breaks such as towelling or retrieving the ball from outside the playing area.

text: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: if any game lasts 10 minutes the remaining games of the match will be played under expedite
expedite begins when any game reaches 10 minutes unless each player or pair has 9 or more points; expedite continues until the end of the match
if time is called when the ball is not in play, the player that received in the previous rally serves the first point in expedite
all other answers presented are correct
correct: if time is called when the ball is not in play, the player that received in the previous rally serves the first point in expedite
note: Rule 2.15.3: If the ball is not in play when the expedite system comes into operation, play shall resume with service by the player who received in the immediately preceding rally.

text: The stroke counter in an expedite rule match counts
options: the server's strokes out loud, calling '13' after he hits his 13th stroke including the serve
the receiver's good returns out loud, calling 'point' when his 13th return hits the table
the server's strokes silently, calling 'point' after he hits his 13th stroke, counting the serve as stroke number 1
the receiver's strokes out loud, calling '13' after he hits his 13th stroke
correct: the receiver's strokes out loud, calling '13' after he hits his 13th stroke
note: HMO 15.2.2: The stroke counter counts aloud the return strokes of the receiving player or pair, from 'one' to 'thirteen', immediately after each stroke. If the 13th return is good, the umpire calls 'stop' and awards a point to the receiver.

text: In the first game of a singles match, with the score at 0-0, A serves to X. The umpire then calls a let because the ball touched the net. Before A can serve again, both player A and player X approach the umpire and request that the rest of the match be played under the expedite system. The player to serve next is
options: A, as the expedite system cannot be introduced until at least 1 point has been scored
A, as no point has been scored
X, as A was the last server
ask the referee for a decision
correct: X, as A was the last server
note: Rule 2.5.3: A let is a rally of which the result is not scored. Rule 2.15.3: If the ball is not in play when expedite comes into operation, the player who received in the immediately preceding rally serves.

text: In a match between A and X, A has just served, and the rally is continuing. The umpire interrupts the rally to introduce the expedite system. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: the umpire should not have interrupted the rally and should only introduce the expedite when the rally has ended
in the next rally A serves to X
in the next rally X serves to A
the umpire tosses a coin to determine if A serves to X or X to A
correct: in the next rally A serves to X
note: Rule 2.15.3: If the ball is in play when the time limit is reached, play shall be interrupted and resume with service by the player who served in the rally that was interrupted.

text: Under misbehaviour regulations
options: the umpire shows a yellow card when giving a warning
the umpire shows a red card when directing an advisor to leave
the umpire shows a yellow and a red card when awarding a penalty point
all other answers presented are correct
correct: all other answers presented are correct
note: Rule 3.5.2.2: yellow card for a warning; Rule 3.5.2.7: red card when sending a warned adviser away; Rule 3.5.2.3: yellow and red card together when awarding penalty points.

text: During the first game A throws his racket into a surround and the umpire gives A a warning, displaying a yellow card. At the end of the game, A kicks a surround. The umpire should
options: again, warn him because the game is over
award a penalty point to X and start the next game with X leading 1-0
call the referee
ignore the incident because A was upset with himself
correct: award a penalty point to X and start the next game with X leading 1-0
note: Rule 3.5.2.3: A second offence earns 1 point for the opponent. HMO 17.3.3: Unused penalty points are transferred to the next game, which starts at 0-1 or 0-2 in favour of the offender's opponent.

text: In the first 2 singles of a team match, A is warned, and B incurs a penalty point. When later in the team match, they are playing as a doubles pair, A intentionally breaks the ball by stepping on it. The umpire should
options: formally warn A/B
award 2 penalty points to X/Y
award 1 penalty point to X/Y
report to the referee
correct: award 2 penalty points to X/Y
note: Rule 3.5.2.6 / HMO 17.3.4: At the start of a doubles match the pair is regarded as having incurred the higher of any warnings or penalties incurred by either player in the same team match, so a first offence in doubles incurs 2 penalty points.

text: In the first 2 singles of a team match, A is warned, and B incurs a penalty point. When later in the team match, they are playing as a doubles pair, A intentionally breaks the ball by stepping on it. What penalties carry forward to each player's next singles match?
options: none
1 penalty point each for A and B
2 penalty points each for A and B
1 penalty point for A, 2 penalty points for B
correct: 1 penalty point each for A and B
note: Rule 3.5.2.6 / HMO 17.3.4: A penalty during a doubles match applies to the pair during that match, but only the offending player carries it over to a subsequent individual match.

text: In the second singles of a team match, B incurs a penalty point. When later in the match A (who has not been penalised before) and B are playing as a doubles pair, B angrily kicks down a surround after losing a point. The umpire should
options: formally warn A/B
award 2 penalty points to X/Y
award 1 penalty point to X/Y
report to the referee
correct: award 2 penalty points to X/Y
note: Rule 3.5.2.6 / HMO 17.3.4: The doubles pair is regarded as having incurred the higher of any warnings or penalties incurred by either player in the same team match.

text: In the second singles of a team match, B incurs a penalty point. When later in the match A (who has not been penalised before) and B are playing as a doubles pair, B angrily kicks down a surround after losing a point. What penalties carry forward to each player's next singles match?
options: none
2 penalty points each for A and B
no penalty for A, 2 penalty points for B
1 penalty point for A, 2 penalty points for B
correct: no penalty for A, 2 penalty points for B
note: Rule 3.5.2.6 / HMO 17.3.4: A penalty during a doubles match applies to the pair during that match, but only the offending player carries it over to a subsequent individual match.

text: In the first 2 singles of a team match, players A and B each are given a warning for misbehaviour. When later in the match they are playing as a doubles pair, A intentionally breaks the ball by stepping on it. What penalties carry forward to each player's next singles match?
options: none
1 penalty point each for A and B
2 penalty points each for A and B
1 penalty point for A, warning for B
correct: 1 penalty point for A, warning for B
note: Rule 3.5.2.6 / HMO 17.3.4: A penalty during a doubles match applies to the pair during that match, but only the offending player carries it over to a subsequent individual match.

text: In the first 2 singles of a team match, A is warned, and B incurs a penalty point. When later in the match they are playing as a doubles pair, A intentionally breaks the ball by stepping on it and X/Y are awarded 2 penalty points. What penalties carry forward to each player's next singles match?
options: none
1 penalty point each for A and B
2 penalty points each for A and B
2 penalty points for A, 1 penalty point for B
correct: 1 penalty point each for A and B
note: Rule 3.5.2.6 / HMO 17.3.4: A penalty during a doubles match applies to the pair during that match, but only the offending player carries it over to a subsequent individual match.

text: After the umpire gives a warning or awards a penalty point the assistant umpire
options: places cards by the scoreboard as directed by the umpire
places a yellow card by the scoreboard after a warning but takes no special action after the award of penalty points
places a red marker by the scoreboard next to the yellow marker after the award of a penalty point
places a red only marker by the scoreboard after the award of a penalty point
correct: places a red marker by the scoreboard next to the yellow marker after the award of a penalty point
note: HMO 17.2.3: After a formal warning a yellow marker is placed near the score indicator; after a penalty point both a yellow and a red marker are placed.

text: In the 1st game of a five-game match, X served first in the match. A is given a warning and for later bad behaviour in the game his opponent, X, is awarded a penalty point. In the 2nd game, A, before serving at the score 10-10, intentionally breaks the ball. The umpire should
options: call for the referee
award X 1 penalty point and continue the game with X serving 11-10
award X 2 penalty points and start 3rd game with X serving 0-0
award X 2 penalty points and start 3rd game with X serving 1-0
correct: award X 2 penalty points and start 3rd game with X serving 0-0
note: Rule 3.5.2.3: For a further offence 2 points are awarded. This makes the score 12-10 to X, ending the game. Since X served first in game 1, X serves first in game 3.

text: In a team match A/B/C vs X/Y/Z, B gives illegal advice to A in the first match and is warned. In the next individual match of the team match, A gives illegal advice to B. The umpire should
options: give A a warning, showing a yellow card
show a red card and require A to leave the area; he cannot return until the completion of the team match
show a red card and require A to leave the area; he can return at the completion of B's match
show a red card and require A to leave the area; he can return only to play his next match
correct: show a red card and require A to leave the area; he can return only to play his next match
note: Rule 3.5.1.4: After a warning, if anyone again gives advice illegally in the same team match, the umpire shall show a red card and send him away, whether or not he was the person warned. Rule 3.5.1.5: The dismissed adviser may return only when required to play.

text: During a team match, between rallies, X's captain keeps calling out to him in a language that the umpire does not understand, and from X's actions the umpire is sure that he is being given advice. The umpire should
options: take no action
take no action, provided he is satisfied that the calls do not disturb A
warn the captain and send him away from the playing area if the calls continue
warn the captain and report to the referee if the calls continue
correct: take no action
note: Rule 3.5.1.3: Players may receive advice at any time except during rallies.

text: Doubles pair A/B are from different Associations and speak different languages. Each player has a separate advisor. In the first game, A's advisor is warned for illegal advice during the game. During the next game B's advisor signals B what serve to use. The umpire should
options: give B's advisor a warning showing a yellow card
show B's advisor a red card and require the advisor to leave the area
show a red card to both advisors and require both to leave the area
take no action
correct: take no action
note: Rule 3.5.1.3: Players may receive advice at any time except during rallies, provided play is not delayed. Since this advice is not given during a rally, it is legal.

text: During a team match advice may be given by
options: anyone on the team bench but only between games
anyone on the team bench but only between games and during authorized suspensions
one designated advisor whenever the ball is not in play
anyone on the team bench whenever the ball is not in play
correct: anyone on the team bench whenever the ball is not in play
note: Rule 3.5.1.1: In a team event, players may receive advice from anyone authorised to be at the playing area. Rule 3.5.1.3: Advice may be given at any time except during rallies. Rule 2.5.1: A rally is the period during which the ball is in play.

text: When one player of a doubles pair is in a wheelchair due to a disability and the partner is standing
options: when serving to the player in a wheelchair the ball must not bounce on the receiver's side and return in the direction of the net
either player can make a return
there is no difference from regular rules
when serving to the player in a wheelchair the ball must not cross the sideline on the receiver's side
correct: when serving to the player in a wheelchair the ball must not bounce on the receiver's side and return in the direction of the net
note: Rule 2.9.1.5.1: Let if the receiver is in a wheelchair and the service, after touching the receiver's court, returns in the direction of the net. The sideline rule in service applies only to singles.

text: In a wheelchair doubles match, A begins the rally by serving to X. During the rally, as A makes a good return, the footrest of his chair crosses the imaginary extension of the centre line of the table. X is unable to make a good return, but his partner returns the ball. The umpire should
options: award the point to A/B because the wrong player returned the ball
take no action because the ball is still in play
award a point to X/Y
declare a let
correct: award a point to X/Y
note: Rule 2.10.1.15: A point is scored if, where an opposing doubles pair includes at least one player in a wheelchair, any part of the wheelchair or a foot of a standing player crosses an imaginary extension of the centre line. HMO Appendix F.

text: In a women's wheelchair doubles match between A/B and X/Y, A serves correctly to X, however the ball goes over the sideline of X's right-hand court. As X makes a good return, she raises her hand appealing for a let which the umpire does not call. B fails to make a good return but in doing so appeals for a let saying she was distracted when X raised her hand. The umpire should
options: allow a let as B was distracted by X raising her hand and advise both players to allow play to continue even if they think the service is a let
allow a let as the ball went over the sideline of X's right-hand court
award a point to X/Y but advise X to allow play to continue even if she thinks the service is a let
award a point to A/B because X caused a distraction
correct: allow a let as B was distracted by X raising her hand and advise both players to allow play to continue even if they think the service is a let
note: Rule 2.9.1.3: Let for a disturbance outside the control of the player. In doubles the sideline rule in service does not apply, so the service was good; however X raising her hand caused a distraction.

text: One player of a doubles pair, player B, is in a wheelchair, and her partner, player A, is standing. During a rally, just as A is making a return, B's foot touches the floor. The umpire should
options: call let and caution B that her foot must not touch the floor
award a point to X/Y as B's foot touched the floor during the rally
award a point to X/Y because B caused a distraction
take no action
correct: take no action
note: Rule 2.10.1.14.3 applies only if both players or pairs are in wheelchairs. Since not all players are in wheelchairs, it does not apply. HMO Appendix F.

text: In a doubles match X, a standing athlete, serves to A, who is in a wheelchair because of a disability. The service, which is otherwise good, bounces in A's right half court and then goes off the side of the table. A returns the ball and Y misses the subsequent return. The umpire should
options: award a point to A/B
award a point to X/Y
call a let
take no action
correct: award a point to A/B
note: As it is a doubles match, the ball crossing the sideline in service only applies to singles matches, so the service was good.

text: X fails to make a good return and the umpire awards a point to A. X protests that A accidentally struck the ball twice and A agrees, although the umpire does not think he did so. The umpire should award a
options: point to X, because both players agree that the original decision was wrong, and the umpire is not certain
let, because the umpire is not certain whether A struck the ball twice
point to A because a decision once made cannot be changed
point to A, because even if A did strike the ball twice it was not deliberate
correct: point to A, because even if A did strike the ball twice it was not deliberate
note: Rule 2.10.1.7: A point is lost only if a player deliberately strikes the ball more than once in succession.

text: The assistant umpire raises his hand and calls 'side' to indicate that the ball returned by X hit the side of the table nearest to the assistant umpire, but the umpire is sure it touched the top edge. The umpire should
options: call let because the assistant umpire's call could have affected the players
call let because he and the assistant umpire disagree
award a point to A because the assistant umpire has the final decision
award a point to X because the umpire has the final decision
correct: award a point to A because the assistant umpire has the final decision
note: Rule 3.3.2.4.1 / HMO 12.2.3: The assistant umpire is solely responsible for edge ball decisions at the side of the table nearest to him or her.

text: After the assistant umpire calls 3 faults against one player the player protests that the assistant umpire is not interpreting the service law correctly. The player wants to appeal to the referee. The umpire should
options: stop the game and call for the referee whether or not the umpire agrees
ask the player to continue or face penalties under the point penalty system
show the player a yellow card and ask the player to continue immediately
call the referee if the umpire agrees the assistant is making mistakes interpreting the service law
correct: stop the game and call for the referee whether or not the umpire agrees
note: HMO 4.6.1: A player, or in a team match his or her captain, may appeal against what he or she believes to be a wrong rule interpretation by the umpire, assistant umpire or stroke counter.

text: In an individual match a player can appeal
options: to the referee against an umpire's interpretation of the service rule
to the umpire against an assistant umpire's decision that his return missed the side of the table nearer to the assistant umpire
to the umpire against a stroke counter's error in counting strokes
to the umpire against an assistant umpire's decision that he struck the ball in service while it was above the table
correct: to the referee against an umpire's interpretation of the service rule
note: HMO 4.6.1: A player may appeal against what he or she believes to be a wrong rule interpretation by the umpire, assistant umpire or stroke counter.

text: In a team event an appeal can be made
options: only by the individual participating in the match during which the appeal has arisen
only by the advisor of the team making the appeal
only by the captain of a team participating in the match in which the question has arisen
by the individual if his captain so agrees
correct: only by the captain of a team participating in the match in which the question has arisen
note: Rule 3.3.3.6: In a team event an appeal may be made only by the captain of a team participating in the match in which the question has arisen.

text: At the end of a rally the umpire should
options: call the score immediately the ball is out of play
signal the result immediately the ball is out of play but delay calling the score until the players are ready to start the next rally
delay the signal and the calling of the score until the players are ready to start the next rally
signal the result immediately the ball is out of play but may delay calling the score until she is satisfied that the players will be able to hear it
correct: signal the result immediately the ball is out of play but may delay calling the score until she is satisfied that the players will be able to hear it
note: HMO 18.1.2: The score should normally be called as soon as the rally is decided, but with loud applause or a player retrieving the ball the umpire may delay slightly until both players can hear it. Appendix A 15: Signal the result, then call the new score as soon as practicable.

text: After the first game the assistant umpire
options: changes the score indicator immediately, changing the game score then changes the points scores to 0-0
changes the score indicator immediately, changes the points scores to blank then changes the game score
changes the score indicator just before the players return for the next game, changing the points scores to blank then changes the game score
changes the score indicator just before the players return for the next game, changing the game score then changes the points scores to blank
correct: changes the score indicator just before the players return for the next game, changing the points scores to blank then changes the game score
note: HMO Appendix A 22: Just before the players return for the next game, set the points score indicators to blank and alter the games score indicators to reflect the result of the previous game.

text: In a match played under the expedite system, the players speak different languages and cannot agree on a language suitable to both. The stroke counter should call the number of strokes in
options: English or in any other language acceptable to the players and the umpire
the language of the Association organizing the event or in English
one of the ITTF official languages
any language decided by the referee
correct: English or in any other language acceptable to the players and the umpire
note: Rule 3.4.1.3: The score and, under the expedite system, the number of strokes shall be called in English or in any other language acceptable to both players or pairs and to the umpire.

text: Player A did not bring his racket to the Call Area before the match but gives it to the umpire in the playing area before the start of the match. What are the tasks of the umpire with regards to this racket?
options: the umpire does a visual inspection of the racket (e.g. damage to coverings and blade, any other irregularity)
the umpire tests the racket in the field of play (thickness, flatness, LARC and any other irregularity)
the umpire does a visual inspection of the racket (e.g. damage to coverings and blade, any other irregularity) and collects the racket after the match for an after-match test
no inspection by the umpire at the table, but the umpire collects the racket after the match for an after-match test
correct: the umpire does a visual inspection of the racket (e.g. damage to coverings and blade, any other irregularity) and collects the racket after the match for an after-match test
note: ITTF Call Area and RCC Workflow: If a racket has not been tested before the match, the umpire does a visual inspection. Rackets not presented before the match will always be tested after the match.

text: In a Class 4 singles match, during a long rally, one of the small wheels falls off from A's wheelchair, which had 2 small and 2 large wheels. The umpire should
options: call let and have the wheelchair repaired before continuing the match
call let and ask A to replace the broken wheelchair with another wheelchair right away
award a point to X as A's wheelchair is missing a wheel
allow the rally to continue
correct: allow the rally to continue
note: HMO Appendix F: Wheelchairs must have at least two large wheels and one small wheel at the start of and throughout a rally. The wheelchair still has one small wheel, so it is legal.

text: In a Class 5 doubles match, A makes a good serve to X. In making the return with a forehand smash, X lifts his right thigh off his wheelchair. A's wheelchair crosses the imaginary extension of the centreline of the table as he returns the ball. The umpire should
options: award a point to A/B as X fails to maintain minimum contact with the seat of his wheelchair
do nothing and let the rally continue
award a point to X/Y as B should be the one to return the ball from X
award a point to X/Y as A's wheelchair crossed the imaginary extension of the centreline
correct: award a point to X/Y as A's wheelchair crossed the imaginary extension of the centreline
note: Rule 2.10.1.15: A point is scored if any part of the wheelchair or a foot of a standing player of the opposing pair crosses an imaginary extension of the centre line. HMO Appendix F.

text: In a wheelchair singles match between A and X, A lifts his body from his wheelchair such that neither of his thighs make contact with the wheelchair seat after making a good return to a wide ball. X fails to make a good return. The umpire should award a
options: point to X because A failed to maintain contact with his chair
point to A because X failed to make a good return as A lifted his thighs off the seat only after striking the ball
let and warn A to maintain contact with the seat of his chair
point to A but warn him to maintain contact with the seat of his chair
correct: point to A because X failed to make a good return as A lifted his thighs off the seat only after striking the ball
note: Rule 2.10.1.14.1 / HMO Appendix F / HMO 12.1.6: Minimum contact with the seat with the back of at least one thigh is required when the ball is struck. Here the thighs were lifted after striking the ball.

text: In a singles match of a Para tournament, player A requests an injury break as he is unable to play temporarily due to the nature of his disability. The umpire should
options: not allow the injury break as the disability was already present at the start of the match
allow the shortest possible injury break because it is necessary to be more considerate towards a player who is disabled
call the referee
not allow the injury break because disabled players are not entitled to request injury breaks
correct: call the referee
note: HMO 13.5.4 / Appendix F: If a player with a disability is unable to play temporarily due to his/her disability, the referee may, after consulting a medical classifier or doctor, allow a recovery time of the shortest practical duration, not more than 10 minutes.

text: In a doubles match, players A and B are in wheelchairs whilst player X, who is in a wheelchair, partners player Y, a standing para player who uses a walking stick for balance. During a rally, player A's racket hand accidentally touches the playing surface just before he hits the ball back over the net. The umpire should
options: call 'let' because A did not deliberately touch the playing surface with his racket hand
award a point to X/Y because A's racket hand touched the playing surface before he hit the ball
take no action and allow the rally to continue
award a point to X/Y and warn A under PPS because he used his racket hand to support himself as he hit the ball
correct: take no action and allow the rally to continue
note: Rule 2.10.1.14.2 applies only if both players or pairs are in wheelchairs. Since not all players are in wheelchairs, it does not apply. HMO Appendix F.

text: During play, X trips over the moving cable of a mobile TV camera and misses the ball. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Declare a let
note: Rule 2.9.2.4: Play may be interrupted because the conditions of play are disturbed in a way which could affect the outcome of the rally.

text: In a rally, while trying to make a return, X's run is blocked by a surround and she fails to make the return. X complains to the umpire saying that the playing area is too small. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to A (or A/B)
note: The size of the playing area is not the umpire's responsibility; it is the same for both players and any complaint should have been made to the referee before the match began.

text: During a rally, A strikes the ball and the ball touches the court of X, who attempts to return the ball but misses it. When X retrieves the ball, he notices it is broken and hands it to the umpire. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to A (or A/B)
note: FAQ 5.7: After the rally a player cannot claim that the ball was broken in the previous rally.

text: A serves and the ball bounces on his side of the table and touches the net, then X touches the playing surface with his free hand before the ball touches his court. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to A (or A/B)
note: Rule 2.10.1.11: A point is scored if an opponent's free hand touches the playing surface.

text: In doubles, as A serves, B stands in such a position that X, who is to receive, cannot see the ball until just before it is struck. X fails to make a good return. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to X (or X/Y)
note: Rule 2.6.4: The ball shall not be hidden from the receiver by the server or his or her doubles partner or by anything they wear or carry.

text: Player A strikes the ball which then bounces close to the net on his opponent's court and the ball bounces high. In an attempt to return the ball X stumbles and his racket falls on the table. He quickly restores his balance by leaning on the playing surface with the hand that just dropped the racket, grabs the racket and manages to return the ball. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to A (or A/B)
note: Rule 2.10.1.11 / 2.5.6: The free hand is the hand not carrying the racket. In this case both hands of player X were free hands.

text: In doubles, A receives but then realises that B should have received. To correct the error, he strikes the ball again when X returns it. Y misses A's return. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to X (or X/Y)
note: Rule 2.10.1.12: A point is scored if a doubles opponent strikes the ball out of the sequence established by the first server and first receiver.

text: When A serves, the ball hits a finger of his racket hand, then his racket, and then bounces on his court, over the net and on to X's court. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Take no action
note: Rule 2.10.1.7: A point is lost only if the ball is deliberately struck more than once in succession. The double hit was accidental.

text: Player A projects the ball high in the air to serve but catches it in his free hand when he sees that it is falling so that he would have to strike it over the table. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to X (or X/Y)
note: Rule 2.5.2: The ball is in play from the last moment it is stationary on the palm before being intentionally projected in service. Rule 2.10.1.1: Point if an opponent fails to make a correct service.

text: During a rally a ball struck by X hits the bracket clamping the net assembly to the table on A's side of the table and falls onto the table. A fails to make a good return. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to X (or X/Y)
note: Rule 2.2.1: The net assembly includes the net, its suspension and the supporting posts, including the clamps attaching them to the table. X made a correct return.

text: X has the ball resting freely on the open palm of his stationary free hand. Then he decides that he would like to serve from another position. As he is changing his position, the ball falls to the floor. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Take no action
note: Rule 2.5.2: The ball is in play only from the last moment it is stationary on the palm before being intentionally projected in service. The ball was not yet in play, so the rally hadn't started.

text: Player A, when serving the ball in a singles match, mishits it. The ball hits the top edge of the end of the table on his side, rises in the air and then, without crossing the net, lands on the net clamp outside the table, and then bounces over the net and lands on X's court. X was distracted by the service action and does not make a return. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Declare a let
note: Rule 2.6.3 / 2.9.1.1: The ball touched the server's court, then the net assembly, then the receiver's court; a service touching the net assembly that is otherwise correct is a let.

text: A, a right-handed shake-hand player, in a desperate attempt to reach a ball on his left-hand side, changes his racket to his left hand, holding the racket by the blade and returns the ball by striking it with the racket handle. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Take no action
note: Players can change racket hand during the rally, and player A has struck the ball with a legal racket.

text: During a doubles rally, B places her free hand on the table to regain her balance just as A, her partner, strikes the ball. The table was not moved, and X misses her return. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to X (or X/Y)
note: Rule 2.10.1.11: A point is scored if an opponent's free hand touches the playing surface. The opponents are both A and B.

text: A catches the ball with his free hand outside the sideline after the ball has travelled across the playing surface on his side without touching the table, but before the ball crosses his end line. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to A (or A/B)
note: Rule 2.10.1.4: Point if the ball passes over the player's court without touching it after being struck by an opponent. The ball is out of play as soon as it passes over the court.

text: X makes a good return and then stumbles and drops his racket. To steady himself, he rests the hand with which he had held the racket on the table, without moving it; A's return misses the table. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to A (or A/B)
note: Rule 2.10.1.11 / 2.5.6: The free hand is the hand not carrying the racket. In this case both hands of player X were free hands.

text: A returns a drop shot, but as he does, he touches the playing surface with his racket hand without moving the table. X misses his next return. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to A (or A/B)
note: Touching the playing surface with the racket hand is allowed.

text: In a doubles match, A, a standing athlete, serves to X, who is in a wheelchair because of a disability. The service, which is otherwise good, bounces in X's right half court and then goes off the side of the table. X makes no attempt to return the ball. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to A (or A/B)
note: Rule 2.9.1.5.3 (let when the service leaves the receiver's court by a sideline) applies only in singles. In doubles the service was good and X did not make a return.

text: In a singles match X, a standing athlete, serves to A, who is in a wheelchair because of a disability. The serve, which is otherwise good, bounces in A's right half court and then goes off the side of the table. A returns the ball and X misses the subsequent return. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Declare a let
note: Rule 2.9.1.5.3: In singles, if the receiver is in a wheelchair and the service leaves the receiver's court by either sideline, the rally is a let as soon as the ball crosses the sideline, regardless of what the receiver does afterwards.

text: In doubles, A serves but X catches the ball saying that it bounced on the wrong half-court, although the umpire is sure that it did not. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to A (or A/B)
note: Rule 3.3.2.3.6: The umpire is responsible for deciding each rally as a point or a let. It is up to the umpire to decide, not the player.

text: The umpire is sure that the ball returned by A missed the table, but A insists that it hit the top edge of the end of the playing surface and X refuses to comment. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to X (or X/Y)
note: Rule 3.3.2.3.6: The umpire is responsible for deciding each rally as a point or a let. It is up to the umpire to decide, not the player.

text: In a match between player A (attacker) vs player X (defender), player X is far behind the table returning the ball. A plays a drop ball and X runs to the table, touches it with his body, moving the surface just a little but did not move the table from its position. X makes a good return that A fails to reach. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to X (or X/Y)
note: HMO 12.1.2: Only lifting, permanent shifting, displacement, or intentional shaking of the tabletop should result in the awarding of a point.

text: In a wheelchair doubles match A serves to X; the service has so much backspin that it touches X's right half court and returns in the direction of the net. X is unable to reach the ball to make a return. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Declare a let
note: Rule 2.9.1.5.1: If the receiver is in a wheelchair and the service, after touching the receiver's court, returns in the direction of the net, the rally is a let.

text: Just as player X, a Class 2 wheelchair player, is about to return a wide angled shot, one wheel falls off his chair and he fails to make a good return. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to A (or A/B)
note: Player X has not made a good return; losing a wheel is unfortunate but not a valid reason for not making a return.

text: In a wheelchair singles match, player A stretches forward and makes a strong smash which player X is unable to return. It was observed that the rear part of one of A's thighs was not in contact with his seat as he struck the ball. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to A (or A/B)
note: Rule 2.10.1.14.1 / HMO 12.1.6: Contact with the seat by the back of at least one thigh is required when striking. Since one of A's thighs was in contact with his seat, it was a good return.

text: In a doubles match, A and X are standing athletes, whilst their partners, B and Y, are in wheelchairs. During a rally, as B makes a return, A's foot crosses over the imaginary extension of the centre line of the table. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to X (or X/Y)
note: Rule 2.10.1.15: Point if any part of the wheelchair or a foot of a standing player crosses an imaginary extension of the centre line. Each player must stay on their own side of the centre line.

text: In a doubles match, two wheelchair players, A and B are playing against a standing player X and wheelchair player Y. During a rally, player X returns the ball twice in succession. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Take no action
note: Rule 2.8.3: In doubles, when at least one player of a pair is in a wheelchair, after the service and the return of service either player of that pair may make returns.

text: In a wheelchair singles match between A and X, A's racket hand touches his side of the table just before he makes a good return. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Award a point to X (or X/Y)
note: Rule 2.10.1.14.2: In wheelchair matches players are not allowed to touch the table with either hand before striking the ball.

text: Standing Para player A uses a walking stick to maintain his balance while playing. In a singles match against X, as A makes a good return during a rally the walking stick slips on the floor causing A to fall onto the floor. X makes a good return. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Take no action
note: The ball is still in play and there is nothing to indicate that A has not subsequently returned the ball.

text: In a wheelchair singles match, A uses the free hand to push onto the wheelchair to get additional leverage and support to return a high ball. What should the umpire do?
options: Award a point to A (or A/B)
Award a point to X (or X/Y)
Declare a let
Take no action
correct: Take no action
note: The ball is still in play and there is nothing to indicate that A has raised his thighs from the chair.
